title: I think I may have clicked a phishing email, what should I do?
description: I clicked an email I thought was from my bank and entered my password, then realized it was fake.

worklogs.description: Guided the user through the password reset steps on a live call.
Opened an incident report with the IT Security team (incident ID: SEC-2024-0317).
Started a CrowdStrike EDR scan, the entire endpoint reported clean.
Revoked all of the user's sessions in Active Directory.
Re-registered the MFA devices (Authenticator + backup phone).
Added the phishing sample to IT Security's weekly security newsletter template.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: 10 minutes ago I clicked an email that came in as 'My Bank', a normal-looking login page opened, and I entered my password. Then the page went blank. Now I've noticed the address isn't bankam.com but bankamtr.com.tr.online... I'm really scared, what should I do?

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Stay calm, you've come to the right person — we'll go through this step by step together. Please close the browser completely NOW. Then: 1) Go to your bank's real website or mobile app (not from the email — type the address yourself), 2) Change your password immediately, 3) Check the recent login records. While you do that, I'll secure your company accounts.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: I closed the browser. I changed my bank password, and there's nothing in the recent login records other than my own device. I'm very happy right now 😅

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Very good, you reacted quickly — that means the attacker hasn't been able to use the account yet. Now for company security: 1) Let's change your company password (corp.local) immediately, 2) I'll re-register your MFA devices (someone may have copied the old one), 3) I'll start a CrowdStrike EDR scan on your computer (it runs silently, won't affect you).

comments.author: agent
comments.message: An incident was reported to IT Security as SEC-2024-0317. Even though the incident appears low-impact, the ticket won't be closed until the process is complete. EDR scan started, awaiting results.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: I changed my company password. What do I need to do for MFA?

comments.author: agent
comments.message: I sent you a 're-registration' link for MFA — when you open your email, click the 'Set up Authenticator' button. In the Authenticator app, delete the old account and add it again (you'll scan a QR code). After this, all your currently active sessions will end and you'll be asked to log in again.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: MFA is done. What will the EDR result show?

comments.author: agent
comments.message: The EDR scan completed, no threats were found on your computer 🎉 The attacker only collected information over the web, no malicious code landed on the device. Incident management is complete: sessions revoked, new password, new MFA, clean EDR. We'd like to add this experience anonymously to our weekly security newsletter — it would be helpful for the team. Would you give us permission?

comments.author: customer
comments.message: Of course, with peace of mind. Let no one else make this mistake again. You acted very quickly and professionally, thank you so much — otherwise I wouldn't have known what to do.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Incident closed, EDR clean, user sessions refreshed. Anonymized use case saved to the security newsletter template. The phishing sample will also be used by the SOC in a retrospective scan.

resolutionNote: Responded quickly after the user clicked a phishing email: 1) The bank side was handled independently by the user, 2) Company password changed, 3) All active sessions revoked, 4) MFA devices re-registered, 5) Endpoint EDR scan clean. Incident impact was zero. The case was anonymized and added to the security newsletter.

csat.comment: I was very scared, but I got a very fast and professional response. The step-by-step guidance was great. Thanks.
